_comment: How the tools of a model call are read as provider-hosted tools, and the /authorize requests the hosted-tool gate makes for them. Shared by the Python and TypeScript SDKs: the Python SDK's tests/test_hosted_tools.py and the TypeScript SDK's tests/hosted-tools.test.ts both check every case. `normalize` cases list the expected HostedTool values (with the resolved action) for a tools list; `requests` cases the same for a whole model request; `mcp_urls` the canonical form of each MCP server URL (null: refused); `registry_refused` lists registries the gate refuses; `requests_refused` values the request normalizer refuses with a type error; `requests_refused_as_instance` requests it refuses with a type error once the value at `path` (`[]`: the request) is made a class instance with the same attributes; `requests_refused_hidden` requests it refuses with a type error once the container at `path` (an object, or a list when `key` is null) hides `key` (or its entries) in each way the language allows a reader to miss what a serializer sends; `gate` cases run against a run handle that allows everything (a case with a `request` goes through the request gate) and list the requests it received. `requests_refused_callable` plants a function in each container of `requests_refused_hidden`, by `variant`: `to_json` drops the hosted key and adds a `toJSON` function that returns the container with it (what JavaScript's `JSON.stringify` sends); `function_value` replaces the hosted key's value with a function; `function_entry_to_json` (TypeScript only, `ts_only`) replaces the first list entry with a function whose own `toJSON` returns that entry. Both lanes expect `TypeError`. Python serializers never call `toJSON` and read a function list entry as a Gemini callable or not at all, so the list variant has no Python counterpart. `callable_names` lists the name of a bare function in a Gemini config and the kind it is read as: `callable:<name>` when the name follows the provider's function-name rule (a letter or underscore, then letters, digits, `_`, `.`, `:` or `-`, at most 64 characters), else `callable` (unknown). `prototype_to_json` (TypeScript only: Python serializers have no such hook) lists the prototypes whose `toJSON` makes the TypeScript lane refuse every request, by `how` it got there: `own` defines it on the prototype, `inherited` gives the prototype another prototype that has it, and `proxy` gives it a `Proxy` as prototype that hides `toJSON` from `has` but returns it from `get` (`Object.prototype`'s prototype cannot be changed). The lane refuses an own `toJSON` on any of the four, and any prototype for `Array.prototype`, `Function.prototype` or `BigInt.prototype` other than `Object.prototype`. The lane checks when it reads the request and again after the decisions, before the gate returns.
